findings.failure_mode: Users see 'exceeded your query concurrency' or 'a lot of queries at the moment' rejections although few queries are running, until leaked slots expire
findings.trigger_condition: getDefaultPeriod/getLimit (platform lookup) throws or times out after the concurrency slot is acquired and before the try block begins
findings.amplifier: Each failed call leaks a slot for the org/project key and the global key. Dashboard auto-refresh and alert evaluators re-issue queries, so more slots leak while the platform lookup stays unhealthy
findings.blast_radius: Queries for the affected project are rejected at its concurrency limit. Under a wide platform outage the global limit can fill and reject queries for all tenants, until the limiter's 5-minute expiry clears the slots

evidence.note: slot acquired before any fallible awaits
awaited getDefaultPeriod/getLimit run outside the try/finally that releases
try begins only after those awaits
stale entries auto-expire after 300s, so the leak self-heals

findings.confidence_rationale: The control-flow gap is visible in the code, but I did not read getLimit to confirm it can throw. The limiter's expiry bounds the impact.
findings.how_to_verify: Stub getLimit to reject, call executeQuery repeatedly with a limit of 2, then check whether later calls get a key_limit rejection.
findings.prediction: Bursts of concurrency-limit errors on dashboards that coincide with platform/billing lookup errors

findings.failure_mode: Every query for a very large org runs two unbounded Postgres scans before ClickHouse is touched, so query latency and DB load grow with the project and environment count
findings.trigger_condition: Org with thousands of projects/environments, with dashboards or alerts issuing frequent queries
findings.amplifier: Auto-refreshing widgets and alert evaluators multiply the per-query Postgres scans, and the full id-to-ref maps are rebuilt in memory each time
findings.blast_radius: Query latency rises for that org and Postgres read load increases for anything sharing the database

evidence.note: project.findMany with no take, run per query
runtimeEnvironment.findMany with no take, run per query
unbounded findMany lead confirmed in code

findings.confidence_rationale: The queries are unbounded and uncached, but real org sizes are unknown and the select is narrow.
findings.how_to_verify: Seed an org with 10k environments and time executeQuery; the Postgres time should grow linearly.
